title.value: Patterns of autism symptoms: hidden structure in the ADOS and ADI-R instruments
title.justification: The paper revisits the Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised (ADI-R) and Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS) with a data-analytics strategy to identify patterns in autism symptoms.
title.quote: We simultaneously revisited the Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised (ADI-R) and Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS) with a comprehensive data-analytics strategy.

analysis.description: This paper employs a comprehensive data-analytics strategy combining pattern-analysis algorithms and extensive data resources on the Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised (ADI-R) and Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS) assessments. It reveals coherent clinical constellations, suggests autism subtypes, examines the predictive power of questionnaire domains, and investigates the impact of demographics like age and sex on these domains. The study emphasizes the significance of certain ADI-R domains in predicting symptom severity and contributes insights to refine autism assessment tools.

type.justification: The study involves empirical evaluation and analysis of data from the ADI-R and ADOS assessments involving 266 patients.
type.quote: Our clustering approach revealed low- and high-severity patient groups, as well as a group scoring high only in the ADI-R domains, providing quantitative contours for the widely assumed autism subtypes.

name.justification: The study is focused on analyzing diagnostic tools and symptom patterns for autism spectrum disorder, a neuropsychiatric condition.
name.quote: We simultaneously revisited the Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised (ADI-R) and Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS) with a comprehensive data-analytics strategy.

name.justification: The paper is centered around autism spectrum disorder and the diagnostic processes involving ADI-R and ADOS.
name.quote: Patterns of autism symptoms: hidden structure in the ADOS and ADI-R instruments

name.justification: The study applies sparse logistic regression to identify the most predictive domains of the ADI-R and ADOS about autism severity.
name.quote: To extract the most informative subsets of domains for predicting autism severity, we capitalized on the pattern-analysis algorithm sparse logistic regression.

is_contributed.justification: Sparse logistic regression is used as a tool for analysis, not as a novel contribution in this paper.
is_contributed.quote: To extract the most informative subsets of domains for predicting autism severity, we capitalized on the pattern-analysis algorithm sparse logistic regression.

is_executed.justification: The study employs this model in its methodology to analyze data from ADI-R and ADOS.
is_executed.quote: To extract the most informative subsets of domains for predicting autism severity, we capitalized on the pattern-analysis algorithm sparse logistic regression.

is_compared.justification: The performance of sparse logistic regression is discussed in the context of its predictive power within the study.
is_compared.quote: Our analysis strategy extracted two of the overall six domains as the most predictive subset and achieved quite effective prediction of autism severity (88.81% accuracy).

referenced_paper_title.value: Statistical Learning with Sparsity: The Lasso and Generalizations
referenced_paper_title.justification: The application and methodology of sparse logistic regression are well-aligned with the principles discussed in this reference work.

name.justification: The study utilizes k-means clustering to identify distinct patient-symptom profiles among individuals with autism.
name.quote: To explore distinct subgroups among individuals with autism, we applied a k-means clustering algorithm to automatically partition patient-symptom profiles into homogeneous groups.

is_contributed.justification: K-means clustering is a well-established method and not introduced as a new contribution in this paper.
is_contributed.quote: To explore distinct subgroups among individuals with autism, we applied a k-means clustering algorithm to automatically partition patient-symptom profiles into homogeneous groups.

is_executed.justification: The k-means algorithm is actively used for clustering analysis in this study.
is_executed.quote: To explore distinct subgroups among individuals with autism, we applied a k-means clustering algorithm to automatically partition patient-symptom profiles into homogeneous groups.

is_compared.justification: The paper compares different configurations and results from applying k-means to determine the optimal number of clusters.
is_compared.quote: Among all metrics of cluster usefulness, and according to the majority rule, the best number of clusters was three.

referenced_paper_title.value: Understanding Machine Learning: From Theory to Algorithms
referenced_paper_title.justification: This textbook provides foundational knowledge on machine learning algorithms like k-means clustering, cited within the research context.

name.justification: The study utilizes the ABIDE dataset for analysis, providing behavioral data for the ADI-R and ADOS assessments.
name.quote: We systematically charted the relationship between the ADI-R and the ADOS based on behavioral data from a publicly available dataset: ABIDE (Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange: https://fcon_1000.projects.nitrc.org/indi/abide/).
